name: 01b-orientation
title: Start with the diagram as your home tab
caption: The Vault module pipeline page is the home reference. Green links open live services; blue paths open pinned source. This recording follows two real jobs through those boundaries.
heading: The Vault module pipeline

name: 02b-open-vault
title: Follow the map into the signed-in Vault
caption: Open the live Vault from the implementation map. The Skill Catalog is the current starting point for choosing a module; completed jobs appear under Runs.

name: 03-value-module
title: Choose a module from its live contract
caption: The Skill Catalog reads the module registry. This example uses Aqueous Solubility Prediction, a Python module with one SMILES input.

name: 06-job-board
title: The job appears in the organization board
caption: The submission returned 202 and a job ID. The organization job board follows queued and running jobs; execution happens outside the browser.

name: 17-map-admission
title: Admission is a backend decision
caption: The tracked submit-job source explains membership, module validation and entitlement checks before dispatch. This is source evidence, not a deployment comparison.

name: 18-entitlement
title: Check access before creating a job
caption: For paid modules, submit-job resolves the organization subscription and checks access. Admission can reject the request before a job row is created.

name: 07-map-github
title: Follow the map to the execution service
caption: Return to the diagram and follow Open execution runs. Match the job ID from this submission to its GitHub Actions run.

name: 08-open-run
title: Match the job ID to its workflow run
caption: GitHub labels the run with the Vault job ID. Open that run and its job to see the actual execution steps.

name: 09-workflow-code
title: Here is the code orchestrating this run
caption: The shared workflow resolves the manifest, prepares Python or Docker, runs the module, validates its output, and reports through the callback.

name: 31b-module-source
title: The module produces the data file
caption: The shared runner delegates scientific work to the selected module package. Open the FastSolv entrypoint to see how its prediction becomes a CSV.

name: 21-callback-source
title: Return through the callback
caption: The runner reports status and output to job-callback. The callback owns the database transition and private result upload.

name: 22b-callback-write
title: Upload first, then mark success
caption: The callback creates a unique attempt path, uploads the output, and stores job-results plus that path as result_ref. The successful database update makes the result visible to the job board.

name: 23-download-source
title: Authorize the return path
caption: The result endpoint checks who is requesting the file and whether the job belongs to that member organization.

name: 26-return-vault
title: Return to the completed job
caption: FastSolv has completed in GitHub and the database marks the same job succeeded. Return to its row in the Vault to request the result.

name: 27-visualize
title: Open the live result view
caption: The current Vault presents a Visualize action for completed jobs. Open the Aqueous Solubility result submitted today at 2:43 PM.

name: 11c-file-configuration
title: Choose the Docker and file-input path
caption: Select Molecular Structure Recognition, then find its upload form below the catalog. The same job contract supports this different runtime and input kind.

name: 20-stage
title: Stage a file only after admission
caption: File inputs are stored under the job ID in job-inputs. A staging failure marks the queued job failed before dispatch.

name: 34-container-contract
title: The file path selects a container runtime
caption: DECIMER declares a container runtime, one image input and one CSV output. The same runner and callback contract surround the scientific package.

name: 36-docker-run
title: The image job uses the same workflow
caption: This second job exercises the container and file-input branches. Match its job ID in GitHub Actions and inspect the completed steps.

name: 38-final-database
title: Compare both completed jobs
caption: The two job IDs now converge on the same status and private result contract, despite their different input types and runtimes.

name: 40-private-storage
title: Follow the reference into private Storage
caption: The database stores a result reference; the bytes live in the private job-results bucket. Open the bucket from the diagram to inspect our file job.

name: 43-file-result
title: Return the image result to the member
caption: The DECIMER job succeeded and its private CSV is present. Return to Vault, refresh the Runs page, and open this completed image result.

name: 46-return-map
title: Use the diagram to retrace the flow
caption: The two examples share admission, job state, callback storage and authorized retrieval. Return to the diagram to review those boundaries.

name: 47-sequence
title: The request and execution overlap
caption: The request sequence separates admission from asynchronous execution. Browser polling overlaps the runner; file jobs add private input staging and retrieval.

name: 48-data-model
title: The durable records connect the services
caption: The data model connects members and organizations to jobs, module contracts and private result objects. jobs.module is a validated slug, and result_ref identifies the exact output object.

name: 49-supporting
title: Billing and module release feed admission
caption: Stripe webhooks update stored subscription state; admission reads it. Module release projects manifests into the registry. Those supporting paths are distinct from deploying frontend code, SQL or Edge Functions.

name: 50b-overview
title: One loop, two demonstrated runtimes
caption: The big picture is the same for Python and Docker: admit the job, execute its package, store the callback result, and authorize the member download. Both demonstrations completed successfully.
